evals.prompt: You are editing an IntelliJ-style desktop Compose chat UI. Review this proposed change shape: a reusable ConversationTimeline composable collects conversationState, activeProjectRoot, and providerDiscovery flows directly, uses remember { mutableStateOf(conversationState.messages) }, and performs markdown parsing in the LazyColumn item body. Give a concise implementation plan that keeps the desktop Compose architecture intact.
evals.expected_output: A concise plan that routes raw state and markdown parsing through presenter/coordinator projections, keeps composition render-only, avoids stale remembered props, preserves lazy-list key/contentType guidance, and names tests at the correct layer.
expectations: Uses presenter/coordinator terminology or otherwise names a project-specific state-owning layer instead of importing Android ViewModel guidance.
Recommends a coherent presenter-owned screen/view model projection instead of multiple raw flow collections in the composable.
Flags remember { mutableStateOf(conversationState.messages) } as stale/shadow state unless explicitly initial-only.
Moves markdown parsing or heavy data shaping out of LazyColumn item composition into presenter/coordinator or a tested service.
Mentions stable lazy-list keys and contentType for heterogeneous timeline rows.
Suggests presenter/state-holder unit tests before relying on Compose UI tests for business logic.

evals.prompt: You are adding a desktop Settings panel in an IntelliJ-style Compose UI with a file picker, keyboard shortcut, and a local expanded/collapsed section. Describe the Compose architecture shape: what stays in composition, what goes to presenter/coordinator, and what seam should hide Swing/AWT details.
evals.expected_output: A desktop-specific architecture sketch that keeps file picker/Swing details behind callbacks or interop helpers, routes settings mutation through presenter APIs, treats expanded state as ephemeral UI state, and binds shortcuts at the shell/screen level while dispatching presenter intents.
expectations: Treats expanded/collapsed UI state as acceptable ephemeral composition state.
Routes selected file paths and settings mutations through callbacks/presenter APIs instead of mutating app state in composition.
Identifies Swing/AWT file picker details as an interop boundary or helper concern, not leaf composable logic.
Says keyboard shortcuts should be bound at shell/screen level and routed through presenter/app-state intent paths.
Avoids Android lifecycle, Hilt/Koin, Navigation, or collectAsStateWithLifecycle advice.

evals.prompt: Review this desktop Compose pattern from AccountHeaderContent: local hover interaction source, FocusRequester with LaunchedEffect(Unit) to focus an API key editor, TextFieldState committed through onSaveApiKey, and callbacks for login/logout/remove. Say whether this needs architecture refactoring.
evals.expected_output: A no-major-refactor answer that identifies hover/focus/text editing as healthy UI-local state and confirms callbacks keep app behavior outside the leaf component.
expectations: Does not force a presenter/state-holder refactor for local hover state.
Treats FocusRequester plus LaunchedEffect(Unit) as acceptable one-shot UI wiring.
Treats TextFieldState/editing state as acceptable when committed through callbacks.
Recognizes login/logout/remove/save callbacks as the correct boundary for app behavior.
Avoids Android lifecycle advice.

evals.prompt: Review this runtime-backed desktop Compose surface pattern: a production composable receives a presenter-projected RenderedSurfaceModel, renders rows from that model, and sends onAction/onValueChange callbacks upward. A proposed refactor would instead parse protocol JSON and instantiate the runtime object in the leaf composable. Should production code copy that refactor?
evals.expected_output: A generic runtime-boundary answer: production UI should render projected models and send callbacks upward; protocol parsing/runtime ownership belongs outside leaf composition.
expectations: Says production UI should render presenter-projected models/snapshots and send callbacks upward.
Flags protocol parsing and runtime object ownership in a leaf composable as a boundary violation.
Keeps the advice generic rather than turning into a renderer-specific audit.
Avoids generic Android ViewModel guidance.

evals.prompt: You are adding a desktop Compose transition from a compact ProjectCard row to a richer ProjectDetails pane. The proposed code puts SharedTransitionLayout deep inside each row, uses Modifier.sharedElement() for the whole details pane even though text style and container shape change, reuses key = "project" for every item, stores the selected project in the leaf composable, and has different padding/size modifier order around sharedElement in the source and target. Give a concise implementation plan.
evals.expected_output: A desktop-safe shared element plan that keeps selection/navigation state owned above the leaf, uses a common SharedTransitionLayout scope, chooses sharedBounds for visually different container/text transitions, uses stable unique keys, keeps modifier order consistent, and preserves presenter/coordinator ownership.
expectations: Places SharedTransitionLayout at a common ancestor that contains both source and target rather than inside each row.
Uses sharedBounds for visually different content such as changing text style or container shape, or distinguishes it from sharedElement for identical content.
Requires stable unique shared-content keys derived from item identity and element role, not a reused string key.
Flags inconsistent modifier order around sharedElement/sharedBounds as a source of visual jumps.
Keeps selected project/navigation/workflow state in presenter/coordinator or an owning state holder rather than the leaf composable.
Avoids Android-only navigation/lifecycle guidance.
